entry.title: docs(web-audio): explain how to add audio effects
entry.content:
Description

Improve the Web Audio API guide by adding guidance on creating and composing audio effects, including a concrete BiquadFilterNode example and a reference to the Voice-change-O-matic implementation.

Motivation

The existing guide explains basic audio graphs and modification nodes, but does not clearly explain how readers can create new audio effects by combining audio nodes. This change provides a practical pattern for adding effects and explains how the Voice-change-O-matic example uses single-node and multi-node effect graphs.

Additional details

The new section covers:

  • Connecting an effect node between an audio source and destination.
  • Combining multiple audio nodes to create more complex effects.
  • Creating a BiquadFilterNode and adding it to an audio graph.
  • How Voice-change-O-matic uses WaveShaperNode, BiquadFilterNode, ConvolverNode, DelayNode, and GainNode to implement different effects.
  • How to add and switch between effect graphs in an application.

entry.title: docs(web-api): document asynchronous task queuing for selectionchange event
entry.content:
Summary

This PR clarifies the dispatch timing of the selectionchange event across Document, HTMLInputElement, and HTMLTextAreaElement documentation.

Per section 3.3 of the W3C Selection API specification, selectionchange is scheduled asynchronously as a task in the user interaction task queue rather than fired synchronously when the selection changes. This behavior differs from many other input/UI events and means listeners fire on the next turn of the event loop rather than within the same call stack.

Closes #45082

Changes Made

  • Document selectionchange event: Added an explanatory note in the Description section describing asynchronous task scheduling.
  • HTMLInputElement selectionchange event: Clarified that selection changes are dispatched asynchronously via the task queue.
  • HTMLTextAreaElement selectionchange event: Updated to maintain consistency across text control docs.

Verification

  • Ran Prettier formatting check across all modified pages.

Signed-off-by: Poorvith M P poorvith007@proton.me

entry.content:
Description

Updated the example. The current example makes it look like the media query detects if an element is overflowing, not how the device handles overflow. I added a paragraph that isn't overflowing, and a note in the CSS to explain that it's about how the device handles overflow.

Motivation

There is a note at the top of the page that explains this, but with the example only showing it working on an overflowing paragraph, which I think a lot of people will skip to, and then assume it will detect overflows. Just wanted to help make it more clear that isn't how this works.

entry.title: Rewrite Content-Digest and Repr-Digest examples with real, verifiable…
entry.content:
… digests

Description

Addresses #45058 (points 3-6) and #45059 (points 5-9): every worked example on both pages either copied values from RFC 9530 without stating the input bytes, used placeholder digests (sha-512=:ABC...=:, [message body]), or was built on the incorrect premise that Content-Encoding causes Content-Digest and Repr-Digest to diverge. Content-Encoding identifies a different representation, so a whole representation sent in one message always produces matching Content-Digest and Repr-Digest values regardless of encoding; real divergence comes from partial responses (Range requests).

Replaced with an MDN-original example body, {"hello": "mdn"}, with every digest value computed and independently cross-verified (Python hashlib and sha256sum/sha512sum, plus a gzip -dc round-trip for the GZIP example). Migrated the fixed Content-Digest examples onto Repr-Digest.

Removed the Want-*-Digest mentions as those are not commonly used in practce and seem like a distraction. They can be handled on the specific relevant pages.

Removed the 406 examples, since they are behavior RFC 9530 doesn't define.

Motivation

The two pages had examples that were confusing, inaccurate or wrong. This change corrects them and makes them consistent on both pages (since they are both inter-related)

Additional details

Relates to #45058 and #45059
